$comment: The single written list of guards this project has earned. Read by scripts/guards.mjs, enforced by skills/doctrine/test/guard-parity.test.ts, rendered into GUARDS.md. Each rule carries `requires`: the traits (scripts/traits.mjs) a skill must declare for the rule to reach it at all — reachability is DERIVED, never typed. `states` names only skills the derivation reaches: `carried` means the skill's own verification script exports that decision function; `owed` is debt. `exceptions` is the third state, for a skill the derivation reaches but which is nonetheless argued not to carry it — a claim with a reason attached, not a restatement of a missing trait, which the derivation already proves on its own. A skill outside the derived set needs no entry anywhere: that blankness is now structural, not argued.

rules.refuses: an asset inlined more than once into a self-contained delivered file
rules.earnedBy: a delivered route scrolly carried the same 340 KiB basemap plate five times — 1.33 MB of a 1.80 MB page, on a beat a newsroom would open on a phone

rules.refuses: a raster plate and the overlay drawn on it fitting differently: cover pairs with slice, contain with meet, fill with none
rules.earnedBy: at 375x812 a plate cropped under an overlay that letterboxed drew Lisbon over Switzerland, at a scale that made every stop a 4px smear. `map-beat` and `map-web` do not reach this rule — neither ships an with object-fit at all, so there is no second projection to disagree with the first: a map beat composites its plate as an inside its own marks' SVG, in their coordinate system, and pairs its ratio against the projected frame instead. That is the same defect reached by this format's other mechanism, which is what plate-geometry-pairing was written for

rules.refuses: a baked plate whose aspect ratio is not the frame its own marks were projected into, so the default xMidYMid meet letterboxes it under them
rules.earnedBy: the same defect projection-pairing names, reached by this format's other mechanism: a map beat composites its plate as an <image> inside the marks' own SVG, where there is no object-fit to disagree with a preserveAspectRatio and the disagreement is between the plate's own ratio and its box

rules.refuses: a baked plate on the opposite luminance side from the ground its beat declares
rules.earnedBy: a beat declared ground #16191B and painted white labels on a dark halo over a dataviz-light plate: furniture correct for its theme, and unreadable
rules.alsoReachedBy: dw-beat, where the surface is not a baked plate but the PNG a delegated renderer hands back. This producer's spec requires an accent and has no field for a ground, so Datawrapper paints on whatever surface its own theme chooses and a story that declared a dark ground can be delivered a white rectangle. Same decision, same tuning constants, different measurement.

rules.refuses: a dash that measures its own path while vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke computes it in screen space, where that length does not live
rules.earnedBy: a river drawn as head, hole and tail because a pattern one route long was measured against a line the camera had scaled up 1.68x; six hours and five wrong diagnoses

rules.refuses: a mark still data-state=pending when the reveal has ended
rules.earnedBy: stop badges kept the fill they were SSR'd with while the line arrived at each of them: the narrative got there and the picture never said so

rules.refuses: two consecutive steps painting the same picture
rules.earnedBy: a five-stop scrolly repainted 4.4 / 0.0 / 0.0 / 0.0 % of its marks across four transitions: one identical picture, five times

rules.refuses: a step whose picture never moves anywhere inside itself, on a beat built to scrub
rules.earnedBy: five finished SSR'd pictures passed every other guard and still jumped at each boundary: the line never drew under the reader's gesture

rules.refuses: nothing on its own: it reads which of the two models a beat is built on, off the markup
rules.earnedBy: an assembly and a scrub owe different things, and guessing which is which misfires on both — the seed's four media have nothing to scrub between

rules.refuses: a ramp whose input range outruns the progress driving it, so the mark it reveals is still arriving when the composition ends
rules.earnedBy: the same defect reached-mark-declares names, reached by this format's own mechanism: a scrolly says a mark arrived by flipping data-state, and a video says it by an opacity ramp. checkTiming already guarantees every NAMED event ends with the composition, so the offender can only be one level down — a ramp over an already-clamped progress whose range ends above 1 never reaches its own end, and the mark it fades in is still fading when the reader's video stops
